findings.one_line: The required zero-in-a-nonconstant-Z-kernel stress witness is not reproduced: this example gives every Z_e singleton support, so it cannot verify the lift on that required case.

The edge-incomplete clause is not consumed by the signed-cell lift or exact-nullity argument (the lift preserves it only to remain in the pre-restricted class); dropping it genuinely broadens the identification theorem without changing its proof.

cited_checks.note: The attested Proposition 2.3 gives null-space orthogonality for identification of the operator-equation functional; the core correctly does not attribute a finite full-data perturbation construction to it.
The attested matroid partition criterion yields the stated standard q-fold union-rank specialization; the graphic substitution r_M(F)=|V|-c(F) is correctly instantiated.
The attested Tutte--Nash-Williams connected-spanning-subgraph characterization is equivalent to the stated edge-disjoint spanning-tree criterion after selecting a spanning tree from each part.
The attested categorical result requires rank k for P(W|Z,x) with k latent categories, supporting the claimed exclusion of rank-deficient kernels from that guarantee.
The attested proposition requires nonempty H and Q in the described two-trial common-comparator setup; the core uses it only as a scope comparison.
The attested exchangeability condition is conditional on observed X, so it does not itself supply transport over the core's latent U.
The attested generalized-inverse differential matches the three-term derivative used by the core; rank separation is explicitly imposed before its local use.
The attested multivariate CLT and delta-method statement support the finite-dimensional invocation after the core establishes smoothness and separation.
The attested real-closed-field quantifier-elimination theorem supports the terminating semialgebraic projection once the core has cleared its positive conditional-probability denominators.
